To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
physical activity is not stable and that there are different patterns of stability depending on the setting and the age of the children.
physical activity indices showed significant, but low stability over 6 years in a representative German sample.
the tracking of physical activity is generally low, and there is a need for more studies that focus on the determinants of change in physical activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and to what extent the physical activity of children is related to their activity as adults.
the question of whether the results of the study are comparable to other studies.
the question whether physical activity can be considered as an indicator of a stable personality trait.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
physical activity is not a stable variable.
physical activity is highly individual and should be considered as a dynamic variable.
the tracking of physical activity in different contexts is low, but not non-existent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tracking of physical activity in adolescents into young adulthood is low and that physical activity is not a stable variable.
the tracking coefficient is low and the change of physical activity is significant.
physical activity in adolescence is an important predictor for physical activity in young adulthood, but not a sufficient one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tracking of physical activity from adolescence to young adulthood was low.
physical activity is not stable over time and that it is necessary to consider this when designing interventions to promote physical activity.
tracking of physical activity from childhood to adulthood is not a given.
